events.message: Executing command: webdev.init_project web, Build an independent production-ready AI-powered personal student academic intelligence platform under original branding, with no impersonation or cloning of any university portal, no university logos or proprietary assets, and no fake university branding. Do not bypass CAPTCHA, authentication, access controls, or security mechanisms; do not scrape against terms or security controls; never store a university password in frontend code or fabricate academic data. Real imported/synchronized academic records are the source of truth. The dashboard must prioritize live authorized data, latest successful sync, user-imported data, user-entered data, and demo data only when explicitly enabled; never mix demo and real data. Academic data synchronization must use only an authorized API, approved university integration, official export, user-provided data, CSV/Excel, JSON, or manual upload. Optional browser-assisted sync is allowed only when explicitly permitted and technically supported. Implement a provider abstraction (AcademicDataProvider) with profile, attendance, timetable, marks, results, assignments, credits, and course materials methods, so a future authorized source can be connected without redesign. Track sync status and last successful sync, log started/completed/added/updated/unchanged/rejected/errors, never claim a failed sync succeeded, retain latest successfully synchronized data on failure, and use transactions so failed sync never overwrites valid records. Provide configurable thresholds and clearly disclose missing or unavailable data. For each subject show total classes, present, absent, current percentage (present/total), required percentage, and scheduled remaining classes. Implement calculators for minimum additional consecutive attended classes to reach the configured threshold, maximum classes missable while remaining above or at threshold, and timetable-based remaining-class projections; label projections mathematical, not official decisions, and report unavailable timetable data honestly. Provide separately configurable extra classes with subject, date, faculty, attendance status, whether they count officially and/or have a separate category; never assume extra classes count. Show official attendance separately from eligible-extra-class projections. Include end-of-semester scenarios: attend every remaining class, miss one per week, miss two per week, and attend regular plus eligible extra classes, with an attendance chart. Categorize subject risk using user-configurable thresholds such as SAFE/WATCH/AT RISK/SHORTAGE, never call them official unless sourced from official rules. Generate attendance-below-threshold, eligibility-reached, and upcoming-risk alerts based only on supplied data. Create a premium responsive personal academic command center with cards for overall attendance, CGPA, credits, subjects, pending assignments, and attendance risk; attendance overview, subject risks, upcoming classes, assignments, recent marks, and AI recommendations; desktop sidebar, mobile bottom navigation (Home, Attendance, Study, AI, Profile), light/dark modes, accessible modern cards, restrained glassmorphism, professional typography, charts, progress, loading/empty states, and toast feedback; avoid childish clutter, excessive gradients/animations, and unsupported statistics. Add a floating AI assistant that retrieves the user's records from the application database before answering questions about attendance, lowest attendance, required/missable classes, attending all remaining or missing the next two, risk subjects, extra classes, CGPA, and pending assignments. Never hallucinate; return a clear insufficient-data response when the records needed are missing. Add Study Material uploads for PDF, PPT/PPTX, DOC/DOCX, TXT, and supported images; organize by subject, unit, topic, and semester. For PDFs, extract text, chunk, embed, store metadata (filename, subject, unit, upload date, page count, content hash), and implement retrieval-augmented generation rather than resending the whole document. Generate important topics, key concepts, definitions, formulas, diagrams, short notes, 5-mark and 10-mark questions, viva questions, and frequently mentioned concepts. Clearly distinguish extracted source content from AI-generated suggestions; never promise exam appearance. Provide chapter summaries, beginner-friendly Easy Mode and concise Exam Mode, document Q&A with source/page references where possible, explanations, examples, exam answers, comparisons, and key points. Provide an automatic study planner connected to attendance, timetable, exam dates, and uploaded material; prioritize exam proximity, weak marks, attendance risk, pending syllabus, materials, and user priorities, without inventing exam dates. Exam Mode must support topics, flashcards, MCQs, short/long answers, viva, practice tests, revision checklists, weak-topic detection, and tracking learned/remaining topics, quiz scores, and revision count. Maintain a personal knowledge base for attendance, marks, timetable, results, assignments, materials, notes, and syllabus. Include API equivalents for student, attendance/analysis/projection, timetable, marks, results, credits, assignments, materials/upload/analysis, AI chat, sync, and sync status; use proper relationships and indexes for students, subjects, attendance, extra classes, timetable, marks, results, credits, assignments, materials, document chunks, study topics, notifications, and sync logs. Preferred stack: React or Next.js frontend, Python FastAPI backend, PostgreSQL, pgvector or Qdrant, configurable LLM provider, local development file storage and cloud object storage in production. Use the available managed web server/database capabilities where needed and preserve a clean adapter boundary if the exact preferred service is unavailable. Secure authentication, password hashing, authorization, environment variables, HTTPS-ready architecture, secure validated and size-limited file handling, no passwords in source, no academic data in public URLs, and no sensitive data in logs are required. This must be an extensible real application, not a static mockup. If there is no authorized university API, deliver a clearly separated provider/import architecture that can later connect to an authorized API or official export, without attempting unauthorized access or credential misuse., {"database":true,"server":true}, acadwise, web-db-user, Nexora Academic Intelligence
